Synopsis:
    Fosun International is relisting Club Med as a standalone IPO targeting $500M+ in proceeds, roughly one year after taking its tourism arm private at a depressed $1.2B valuation. Club Med operates 69 resorts across 40 countries under an asset-light lease model. Despite €57M net profit in H1, the IPO faces headwinds: revenue growth has nearly stalled (+1.3% in FY2025), operating income is declining, and EBITDA margins (~20%) trail peers like Hilton (~30%). Fosun's strategy to pivot toward Chinese outbound travelers is complicated by weak overseas spending growth (+1.4%) despite rising trip volumes. A $3B valuation benchmarked at peer P/E multiples (~23.5x) will be a hard sell given the weaker growth and profitability profile.

Relevance: IMPLICIT — US hospitality peers Marriott and Hilton are used as valuation benchmarks, but the article is primarily about a Hong Kong/European-listed IPO with no direct US market or macro implications.
